title: Forms and Events
subtitle: Handle User Input Like a Pro - From Search to Login to Add Lesson
description: Master controlled components, onChange, onSubmit, form validation, handling multiple inputs, checkboxes, and build real forms: search, add lesson, contact - everything your dashboard needs.

blocks.text: PAGE 1: The Problem - HTML Forms vs React Forms

Hey! In HTML, when you type in <input>, browser automatically keeps the value inside DOM. You read it later with document.getElementById('input').value. In React, we don't want DOM to be source of truth - we want STATE to be source of truth. Why? Because if state holds input value, you can instantly validate, filter lessons live, show character count, enable/disable button - all without touching DOM.

React form pattern is called Controlled Component: Input's value comes from state: value={search}. And onChange updates state: onChange={(e)=>setSearch(e.target.value)}. State -> Input value, Input change -> setState -> new State -> new Input value. Two-way binding via state!
Uncontrolled is old HTML way - DOM holds value, you read via ref. We will use Controlled 99% - it's modern standard for your dashboard search, login, add lesson form.
Open Practical > React editor. We build every form type today.

blocks.question: APPLICATION: You have search input for lessons. You need to show live filtered results as user types. Why controlled component?
options: Because controlled keeps input value in state, you can filter lessons array using search state instantly on every keystroke
Because uncontrolled is faster
You cannot do live filtering in React
Controlled means browser controls value, not React
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly! State holds search -> filter lessons.filter(l=>l.title.includes(search)) -> map -> live results. That's your dashboard search feature!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Controlled = state is source of truth. search state -> filter lessons -> live results update each keystroke.
blocks.reasoning: Controlled components enable instant UI reactions to input changes.

blocks.text: PAGE 3: Handling Multiple Inputs - Your Add Lesson Form Needs 4 Inputs

Your Add Lesson form needs title, learn, summary, status - 4 inputs! You could create 4 useState: const [title, setTitle] = useState(''), const [learn, setLearn] = useState('')... but better way: ONE object state for whole form: const [form, setForm] = useState({title:'', learn:'', summary:'', status:'locked'}). blocks.question: APPLICATION: You have form with 5 fields: name, email, password, age, country. What's efficient way to handle state?
options: Create 5 separate useState hooks and 5 handleChange functions
Create one object state {name:'', email:'',...} and one handleChange using e.target.name to update correct field
Use 5 different forms
You cannot handle 5 inputs in one form
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! One object state + one dynamic handleChange = clean code. This is standard in real companies for large forms.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: One form object + [name]: value pattern handles all inputs with one function. Saves 80% code.
blocks.reasoning: Object state pattern scales to any number of inputs.

blocks.text: PAGE 4: onSubmit - Preventing Page Reload (Critical!)

In HTML, when you submit <form>, browser reloads page and sends data to server - old way. In React SPA (Single Page App), we DON'T want reload - we want to handle submit in JavaScript, add lesson to state, show success message. So we use e.preventDefault() inside onSubmit handler to stop reload!

blocks.question: APPLICATION: You built add lesson form but when you click Submit, whole page reloads and lessons disappear. What did you forget?
options: You forgot e.preventDefault() in handleSubmit to stop browser's default form reload
You forgot to use useEffect
Forms always reload in React, cannot prevent
You need to use uncontrolled components
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly! e.preventDefault() stops reload. This bug happens to every beginner - remember it!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Add e.preventDefault() as first line in handleSubmit. Without it, browser reloads and React state resets.
blocks.reasoning: Preventing default form submission is essential for SPA behavior.

blocks.text: PAGE 5: Validation - Show Errors Before Submit

Real forms need validation: Title required, min 5 chars, learn text required, email must contain @. In React we validate using state: Keep errors object state, check on submit or on change, show error messages conditionally.

blocks.question: APPLICATION: You have checkbox 'Show only completed lessons'. How do you handle its state?
options: Use value property like text input
Use checked property and e.target.checked - because checkbox value is boolean true/false, not text
Checkboxes don't need state in React
Use onSubmit only, not onChange
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! Checkbox = checked={state} and e.target.checked. Text input = value={state} and e.target.value. Different!
blocks.reasoning: Different input types have different properties for controlled pattern.

blocks.question: APPLICATION: User types 'hooks' in search and selects 'locked' filter. You need to show lessons that match BOTH search AND filter. How?
options: Use two separate filters that override each other
Chain filters: lessons.filter(l => l.title.includes(search) && (filter==='all' || l.status===filter)) - must match both conditions
You need backend for filtering
Filtering cannot combine search and status
blocks.correctFeedback: Perfect! && means AND - must match search AND filter. That's how your dashboard's search + filter will work together.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Use && to combine conditions: matchesSearch && matchesFilter. Both must be true to show lesson.
blocks.reasoning: Combining multiple filter criteria is common real-world requirement.

options: Only useState for one input
Object state for all fields, [name]: value for dynamic update, checked for checkbox, e.preventDefault in handleSubmit, errors state + validate(), map to show feedback list
You need backend for validation
Forms cannot be built with React
blocks.correctFeedback: PERFECT! You just described full professional form architecture - that's exactly what real companies use. You're ready for Lesson 10 complete app!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Full form needs: Object state, dynamic handleChange, preventDefault, validation, errors state, and display list. All concepts from today combined.

blocks.question: BUG FIX: You typed in input but value doesn't show, stays empty. You wrote <input onChange={(e)=>setSearch(e.target.value)} /> without value prop. What's wrong?
options: You forgot value={search} - without value prop it's uncontrolled, React state and input are not synced, it becomes uncontrolled component
You need to use useEffect
onChange is wrong event
Input cannot be controlled
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! Controlled needs BOTH value={state} AND onChange. Missing value = uncontrolled = state not driving UI.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Controlled component requires value={search} + onChange. Without value prop, input is uncontrolled and state doesn't control display.
blocks.reasoning: Understanding controlled vs uncontrolled prevents common form bugs.
